messages.subject: ModAvgPred Function Question
parts:
Hello fellow unmarkers,

I have a rather convoluted question. I have a covariate, drainage area (referred to  as "DA" in r-script, and raw data),that I'm using to  aid in the calculation of the probability of occurrence of a rare stream fish. My expectation, based on the raw presence/absence data, would be that the probability of occurrence at a site would decrease as cumulative drainage area increases. Based upon the raw data, the species definitely appears to occur more frequently in streams with a smaller upstream drainage area.  However, upon plotting the predicted values (produced using the ModavgPred function) the exact opposite appears to be true instead (i.e., probability of occurrence for this species increases as drainage area at a site increases). I'm currently unsure if there's something I doing incorrectly, in terms of my code, or not. I suppose it's feasible that I'm not doing anything incorrectly, and that the predicted values are correct. 

Here was my flow in terms of r-script, with actual r-script and the raw data posted below: Upon construction of each initial model, I selected models for model averaging based upon a delta AIC of <4. I then used the MacKenzie-Bailey GOF test to assess c-hat, so that I could account for overdispersion and  calculate QAIC. Upon doing this, I then used the modavCustom function to determine the average estimates for both detection and probability of occurrence. Finally, I created a newdata object, so I could control for the effect of each covariate, except for the one I was interested in, so I could then predict this variable's  influence on probability of occurrence. At the end of the code, I'm simply plotting the relationship, based off of the predicted values.

For the record, I realize what I'm asking is very complex, but I've reached my wit's end trying to understand what is going on.  Therefore, any help would be greatly appreciated!

Regards,

Josh

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: RE:[unmarked] ModAvgPred Function Question
parts:
Hi Joshua,

here are few comments:

1) it's often a good idea to standardize your covariates before analysis. You seem to have attempted to use scale( ) , but it won't take effect unless you store the results in the object.

2) If you create a named list of models, i.e., list("yd1" = yd1, "yd2" = yd2, ...), then you don't need to use the modnames argument - aictab( ) and related functions will just use the names you specified in the list.

3) What was the c-hat value you obtained from the GOF test? You want to use the value you obtained from the global model, provided c.hat > 1, but not too much (e.g., 3 or 4). You will also want to use this value to get predictions with modavgPred( ).

4) If you have models with covariates on psi or p, then it is a bit strange to compute an average value of psi or p, especially if some models with covariates have a lot of support. It would be more meaningful to compute predictions of psi or p in relation to some values of your variables of interest. 

5) The whole point of multimodel inference is using the entire model set so that models with a lot of support will have the greatest contribution to your estimate. You don't need to chop down the model list, just use modavgPred( ) to make predictions using the entire model set - the models without support won't contribute to the predictions.

Hope it helps,

Marc
